evals.name: context-menu-file-action
evals.prompt: We have a pile of .md files in DocSpace from the tech writers, and it is awkward for people - to see the rendered markdown you have to download the file first. I want a plugin: right click on a .md file → a "Preview as HTML" item, opens a modal with the rendered content. Our portal is self-hosted, version 3.7.
evals.expected_output: A built plugin project with ContextMenu + API scopes, dist/plugin.zip present, validator clean. Item filtered to .md files, opens a modal, handles fetch failures.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors
package.json depends on @onlyoffice/docspace-plugin-sdk ^2.1.0, not 3.x
declared scopes include ContextMenu and are all implemented
the context menu item is restricted to .md files via fileExt with fileType including file
items are registered inside onLoadCallback, not at module scope
the item key is namespaced with the plugin name
window.Plugins.<X> matches pluginName in package.json exactly
the modal is opened via showModal with modalDialogProps present in the same message
the modal object defines onLoad, which the SDK marks as required
network or parsing failures are caught and surfaced to the user rather than left to reject

evals.name: settings-and-info-panel
evals.prompt: need a plugin for docspace that shows in the info panel tab how much space a room takes up and who owns it. and so the admin can set a threshold in gigabytes in the settings, above which the size is highlighted in red
evals.expected_output: A built plugin with InfoPanel + Settings + API scopes. Settings persist via saveSettings and are read in setAdminPluginSettingsValue, not during onLoadCallback. Info panel content loads via onLoad, not in onLoadCallback.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors
declared scopes include InfoPanel and Settings and are all implemented
saveSettings is returned only from the settings save button
setAdminPluginSettingsValue parses the stored string defensively, inside try/catch
stored settings are not read during onLoadCallback, where they are not yet available
info panel content is fetched in the item's onLoad rather than in onLoadCallback
if the info panel item filters by user role it uses usersTypes, the plural form
items are registered inside onLoadCallback
window.Plugins.<X> matches pluginName in package.json exactly

evals.name: audit-broken-plugin
evals.prompt: This plugin builds and uploads to the portal fine, but there is nothing from it in the interface at all. Have a look at what is wrong.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the pluginName/window.Plugins mismatch as the root cause. Should also catch the usersType/usersTypes error, the dead action without payload, and items registered outside onLoadCallback.
assertions: identifies the registration mismatch (window.Plugins.RoomStatistics vs pluginName RoomStats) as the root cause of nothing appearing
flags usersType on the ContextMenu item, where the host reads usersTypes
flags the showModal action returned without modalDialogProps, which makes the click dead
notes that items are registered at module scope instead of inside onLoadCallback
does not modify the plugin, since the user only asked what was wrong
cites concrete file and line locations
explains findings in terms of observable symptoms, not just contract violations

evals.name: extend-existing-plugin
evals.prompt: Here is our plugin with room notes, it is already installed on the portal and works. Right now the note is only visible through the context menu, which is an extra click. Please add it so it also shows up in the room's info panel tab - just as text, no need to edit it from there.
evals.expected_output: The existing project is extended in place: InfoPanel added to scopes and implemented together, version bumped, name and pluginName untouched, the existing context menu item still registered, project rebuilt and validating clean.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists and was rebuilt after the edit
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors
InfoPanel is added to package.json:scopes and implemented in the same change, with at least one item registered
name stays room-notes and pluginName stays RoomNotes, since the portal keys the installed plugin by them
version is bumped above 1.2.0, without which the portal serves the cached bundle
the existing room-notes-edit context menu item is still registered and still works
the new item key is namespaced with the plugin name and does not collide with the existing one
the info panel item reads its content in its own onLoad rather than in onLoadCallback
the project's existing conventions are followed - labels go through locales.ts rather than being hardcoded
the plugin is extended in place rather than regenerated from the scaffolder

evals.name: ui-modal-form
evals.prompt: I want a plugin: a "Send to archive" item in the main button, which opens a little window with a field for the archive URL and a dropdown for the format (zip / tar.gz), and a "Send" button. If the URL is empty or does not start with https, a red message should appear under the field right away, and the button should not send anything.
evals.expected_output: A built plugin with MainButton scope whose modal body is a declarative component tree. Live validation via updateProps on the input and updateContext on the error label. Every node carries the props its component cannot render without.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors, and no findings with code component
every node in the tree is shaped as { component, props } using the Components enum
the button node carries label, size and onClick, which the host cannot render without
the input node carries value and onChange, and the comboBox carries options and selectedOption
ButtonSize is used as an enum member rather than a bare string, which the SDK's const enum rejects
modalDialogProps carries displayType, dialogHeader, dialogBody, onClose and onLoad
the modal onLoad returns every section the dialog has - the host assigns header, body and footer together, so returning only newDialogBody wipes the rest
the comboBox options are objects with key and label, labels are unique, and selectedOption is kept in sync via updateProps from onSelect
the error text uses var(--input-error-color) rather than a hardcoded red or the nonexistent --error-color
the error label is addressed by contextName and updated with updateContext, not by rebuilding the tree
the input updates itself with updateProps in the same message that updates the error label
validation lives in the callbacks rather than being described in prose to the user

evals.name: explain-filter-fields
evals.prompt: Hey, how do you restrict an item by user role in a docspace plugin? I saw usersType in one place and usersTypes in another, and both seem to compile. Which one is right, and why is it like that?
evals.expected_output: A direct answer: both are real, the correct one depends on the scope, and the singular/plural split is a portal quirk rather than a rule. Names which scopes take which, and warns that the wrong one compiles and then silently shows the item to everyone. No project is generated.
assertions: answers directly instead of generating a project, since the question asked for an explanation
states that both field names are real and that which one applies depends on the scope
names the scopes on each side of the split rather than answering only for one
labels it a portal inconsistency rather than presenting it as a designed rule
explains the observable consequence - the wrong spelling compiles, installs, and the filter silently does nothing
answers from the reference files rather than from recall, and does not invent a field or a scope
mentions how to check it - the validator reports the wrong field for that scope

evals.name: native-looking-settings
evals.prompt: make a plugin for docspace: in the plugin settings a "Webhook URL" field, an environment dropdown (Production / Staging), a "send notifications" toggle and saving. important that it looks like the portal's own settings - in dark theme too, half the team is on dark
evals.expected_output: A built plugin with the Settings scope whose settings block matches the portal's visual language: comboBox options as {key, label} objects kept in sync via updateProps, the toggle wrapped so it has real dimensions, colors via theme variables or defaults (no hardcoded hex), saveSettings from the save button, stored settings parsed defensively.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors and zero component warnings (no dead sizes, no malformed comboBox options)
Settings scope is declared and implemented, with a saveButton whose onClick returns saveSettings plus the serialized settings string
the comboBox options are {key, label} objects with unique labels, selectedOption is one of them, and onSelect returns updateProps with the new selectedOption
the toggleButton onChange takes no arguments and flips isChecked via updateProps
the toggle is wrapped in a box with explicit dimensions, since the control has no intrinsic size and overlaps siblings otherwise
no hardcoded hex colors in component props - theme variables like var(--text-color) or component defaults instead
none of the dead enum values are used: ButtonSize.extraSmall, InputSize.big, InputSize.huge
the input stays controlled - onChange returns updateProps with the new value
setAdminPluginSettingsValue parses the stored string defensively and tolerates null after the plugin was disabled
items are registered inside onLoadCallback and window.Plugins.<X> matches pluginName

evals.name: plugins-switched-off
evals.prompt: we uploaded this plugin to our own docspace, reloaded the page like the docs say, and there is nothing. no item in the context menu, nothing in the console either. our admin says the archive uploaded fine. can you find what is wrong with it? we need it working today
evals.expected_output: The plugin is correct and must not be changed. The answer is that the portal's plugin system is a server setting that is off by default - when enablePlugins is false the portal never calls initPlugins(), so no bundle is fetched and nothing is logged. Names pluginOptions.upload/delete as the neighbouring switches, and says this is portal configuration the plugin author cannot fix.
assertions: does not report a defect in the plugin, because there is none - the fixture validates clean
names the portal-level switch (enablePlugins, from the server's plugins.enabled)
says it is off by default, so a fresh self-hosted portal shows this exact symptom
explains the silence: with the flag false the portal never calls initPlugins, so there is no bundle fetch and nothing in the console
mentions pluginOptions.upload / pluginOptions.delete as separate switches, and that a portal can run plugins while refusing new ones
says this is server configuration rather than something the plugin or its author can fix
does not modify the plugin
checks the plugin before blaming the portal, rather than guessing - runs the validator or reads the source

evals.name: background-job-progress
evals.prompt: our users export whole rooms to our storage and it takes a few minutes. right now they have to keep a dialog open the whole time or they lose track. can you make a docspace plugin where they start the export from the main button and then see how far along it is, like the portal shows its own downloads?
evals.expected_output: A built plugin with MainButton + API scopes that reports progress through the portal's floating operations button rather than a held-open modal: addFloatingOperationsButton with an operations array, updates via updateFloatingOperationsButton, removal by the bare id string.
assertions: dist/plugin.zip exists
validate-plugin.mjs --invoke reports zero errors
progress is reported through Actions.addFloatingOperationsButton rather than by keeping a modal open
floatingOperationsButtonProps carries an id, which is the handle every later update and the removal are keyed by
each operation carries id, label, operation, alert and completed - the host reads all of them
operation is a FloatingOperationType member, with Other for a job that is not one of the portal's own
progress is advanced with Actions.updateFloatingOperationsButton, not by adding the button again
removeFloatingOperationsButton is passed floatingOperationsButtonPropsId as a bare string, unlike every other action's payload
the icon on an operation is an asset file name, not a URL
network failures mark the operation with alert rather than leaving it stuck at a percentage
items are registered inside onLoadCallback and window.Plugins.<X> matches pluginName
